title: Philly Cheesesteak Sliders For a Tailgate
description: For flavorful, juicy cheesesteak sliders, use thinly sliced skirt steak cooked with caramelized onions and gooey, melted cheese on toasted buns. Slicing the skirt steak against the grain will make it extra tender.
ingredients: 1 - 1½ pounds skirt steak, trimmed of excess fat, maybe cut in half or thirds, etc., so it fits easily in the pan
1 sweet or yellow onion, thinly sliced
1 cup Mornay sauce, made with provolone, American, or even Mexican cheese (not Cheese Whiz), maybe with a little Parmesan added to give a little bite
Salt and black pepper to taste
directions: In a hot pan, sear a nicely salted skirt steak 2-3 minutes on each side for a just barely medium rare finish (it will cook more later in the oven). The timing will vary with the thickness of the steak.
Let it rest and cool for a few minutes, then slice into little bits: first with the grain, then slice the slices into bits. (Try not to sample too many little bites.)

Meanwhile, heat 1 tablespoon of oil and 1 tablespoon of butter in a large skillet over medium heat. Add the sliced onion and cook for 5 minutes, then added the garlic and cook for another 5 to 10 minutes, stirring occasionally until soft and caramelized. Season with salt and pepper, then remove from the skillet and set aside. (You could cook these with some Italian spices, or oregano or thyme too)
Combine the cooked steak and the caramelized onions and a dash of Worcestershire sauce. Then stir in some cheesy Mornay sauce to make a beautiful gooey mixture. Check the seasoning.
(The Mornay sauce is basically 2 Tbs butter, 2 Tbs flower, 1 cup milk, 2-3 slices or equivalent of cheese.)
Slice the package of slider buns in half horizontally (maybe with the bottom a little thicker), keeping the tops and bottoms intact if possible.

Place the bottom half of the buns in a baking dish. Lay 6 slices of provolone cheese over the bottom buns. Top the cheese evenly with the skirt steak, onion, and cheese mixture. Add the remaining 6 cheese slices over the meat. Place the top half of the buns over the meat and cheese.
In a small bowl, melt 1 tablespoon of butter and stir in the garlic powder. Brush the garlic butter generously over the top of the buns.

Cover the baking dish loosely with foil. Bake for 7-10 minutes, or until all the cheese is melted and gooey. Remove the foil and bake for another 3-5 minutes, or until the tops of the buns are golden brown.
